source_a_excerpt: In Radio Free Albemuth the visionary experiences are assigned to the single character Nicholas Brady, with 'Philip K. Dick' present as a separate, sceptical first-person narrator.
source_b_excerpt: In VALIS the same material is split: the narrator 'Phil' and the visionary 'Horselover Fat' are two facets of one person, a doubling the text foregrounds explicitly.
difference_summary: The earlier, abandoned version (Radio Free Albemuth) externalises the visionary onto a separate friend; the rewrite (VALIS) internalises and splits the author-figure into narrator and madman, turning a plot device into the book's central epistemological move.
interpretive_implications: The split-narrator device in VALIS is widely read as Dick dramatising his own uncertainty about 2-3-74; comparing it against the RFA frame shows that uncertainty being built into form rather than asserted.
notes: Excerpts here are paraphrase placeholders; a production artifact would quote short, fair-use spans with page locators. RFA is the posthumously published earlier treatment of the material reworked into VALIS.
